title: Short Stuff: Fish n' Chips
summary: Short Stuff episode on fish and chips ("chippies"). Josh and Chuck trade banter about the name "chips" (short for chipped potatoes) and whether chipped beef is fried, then cover the history of fried fish: Sephardic Jewish immigrants in Spain and Portugal frying fish for Sabbath meals, their spread to England and street selling, and railroads spreading the dish across the UK. They discuss the potato's arrival in Europe from South America, Belgian and Spanish Netherlands fries, competing claims for the first chippy in London and Mossley near Manchester around 1860s, the peak of about 35,000 shops in the 1920s and decline to about 10,000 today, wartime government support for fish and chips in World War One and World War Two, newspaper wrapping that ended in the Thatcher era, and condiments like malt vinegar, curry sauce, mushy peas and tartar sauce. Closes with personal anecdotes about lobster rolls and saltwater taffy in Maine and a plug for the HowStuffWorks article by Dave Roush.
topics: World War One fish and chips rationing
World War Two fish and chips

segments.title: Opening banter and the name 'chips'
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open with banter, explain that British chips are French fries and the name comes from chipped potatoes, joke about chipped beef, and set up the topic of fish and chips.

segments.title: Fish and chips popularity and Maine food anecdotes
segments.summary: They note the UK's chippy boom in the late 1920s with about 35,000 shops, now about 10,000, and 360 million meals a year. They joke about food in Maine and Boston and how they have not eaten much fish and chips.

segments.title: Sephardic Jewish origins of fried fish
segments.summary: The fried fish tradition is traced to Sephardic Jews in Spain, who could not cook from sundown Friday to sundown Saturday for the Sabbath, so they fried battered fish that would still taste good. The practice spread as they were pushed out of Spain and Portugal, and they sold fried fish on streets in England.

segments.title: Mid-episode message break
segments.summary: A short break is announced before the chips are introduced.

segments.title: Potatoes, Belgian fries, and the first chippies
segments.summary: Potatoes reached Europe from South America in the late fifteenth century and were initially disliked. Fried potatoes appeared in Spain in the sixteenth century and spread to the Spanish Netherlands near modern Belgium. Fried potatoes reached Britain around the 1860s and combined with fried fish. London and Mossley near Manchester both claim the first chippy.

segments.title: Wartime fish and chips, newspaper wrapping, and condiments
segments.summary: Fish and chips were kept off rationing during both World Wars, with David Lloyd George in WWI and Churchill in WWII. Newspaper wrapping, which ended in the Thatcher era, is discussed along with malt vinegar, mushy peas, curry sauce, tartar sauce, and personal food anecdotes, followed by a plug for the HowStuffWorks article.
topics: World War Two fish and chips
